newsitem.title: SWEDEN: GOLF-GARRIDO EYES CUP SPOT AS EIGHT TIE FOR LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GARRIDO EYES CUP SPOT AS EIGHT TIE FOR LEAD.

text.p: A remarkable eight-way tie for the halfway lead in the Scandinavian Masters on Friday featured Spanish Ryder Cup hopeful Ignacio Garrido, seeking to follow father Antonio into Europe's team.
Garrido, the recent German Open winner for his first European Tour victory, posted a three-under-par 69 to move to eight-under 136.
He leads jointly with compatriots Jose Rivero and Domingo Hospital, and Englishmen Peter Baker, who had the best second round of 66, Gary Evans and Miles Tunnicliff.
The eight-strong pacemaking group is completed by Swedes Michael Jonzon, who bogeyed the last to deny himself the outright lead, and Joakim Haeggman.

A shot back are Ireland's Padraig Harrington, who can seal his Ryder Cup place with victory this week, and another Englishman, Van Phillips, with Sweden's Ryder Cup wild-card hopeful Jesper Parnevik among those a further stroke back.

Garrido can follow his father, who played for Europe in the 1979 Ryder Cup to become current captain Seve Ballesteros's first pairs partner, by taking one of the 10 automatic team places if he can clinch the 125,000 points on offer for victory this week.
The Madrid professional started quietly with 10 pars but then suddenly burst into life with birdies on the 11th and 12th.
Though he dropped a shot on 14, he joined the leaders with more birdies on 16 and 17, protecting his score with a "banana-shot" around trees on the last to save par.
"It's the first time I've been in contention since winning in Germany," said Garrido, "because after my victory I wasn't too focused.

"Obviously I dream about playing in the Ryder Cup and following my father, but not out on the course. Then I just think about winning this tournament and if I do, the other goal will fall into place because first prize will get me to Valderrama."
Jose Maria Olazabal, who is in the 10th and final automatic qualifying place, shot 74, spending much of his round worrying about a spectator he hit with his ball on his third hole.
Olazabal found out the injured fan had recovered, but the Spaniard is seven off the pace and could be passed by Ryder rivals Garrido and Harrington, who is 11th.
Ballesteros is hoping Olazabal will qualify automatically to leave him with two wild cards to use.
European money-winning leader Ian Woosnam missed the cut by one stroke, while fourth-placed Colin Montgomerie qualified on one under in his quest for a fifth consecutive title as European number one.
